To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ionic conductivities of the polymer electrolytes were enhanced by increasing the amount of plasticizer and by increasing the temperature.
the use of modified natural rubbers in conjunction with PEO as a polymer electrolyte matrix can yield mechanically stable films and good ionic conductivity at room temperature.
the ionic conductivity and mechanical strength of polymer electrolytes based on natural rubber can be enhanced by the incorporation of a small amount of plasticizer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new electrolyte materials for use in lithium batteries.
the development of polymer electrolyte systems based on modified natural rubbers and poly(ethylene oxide).
the development of new polymer electrolytes with improved mechanical properties and thermal stabilities for use in electrochemical devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the modified natural rubber polymer hosts, ENR-25 and ENR-50, have been shown to exhibit ionic conductivies comparable to those of the PEO polymer host, but with the advantage of being more easily fabricated into free standing films and with the added benefit of being less hygroscopic.

the plasticizers used in this study are effective in improving the ionic conductivity of the unplasticized polymer systems, but the improvement in conductivity was at the expense of mechanical stability.
the ionic conductivity of the polymer electrolytes can be improved by plasticization with EC/PC, but that this improvement is not as dramatic as for PEO-based polymer electrolytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ionic conductivity is strongly influenced by both the polymer host and the plasticizer content.
the ionic conductivity of the polymer electrolytes based on ENR-25 is higher than the polymer electrolytes of the same composition based on ENR 50.
ENR/PEO based polymer electrolytes exhibit ionic conductivity comparable to those of PEO/LiClO4 and PEO/LiCF3SO3 systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ENR-25 and ENR-50 are suitable polymer hosts for polymer electrolyte applications.
the use of epoxidised natural rubbers as hosts for polymer electrolyte systems can be considered as a viable alternative to the use of synthetic polymer hosts.
modified natural rubbers can be employed in the fabrication of polymer electrolytes with low glass transitions and that plasticizers such as EC/PC can enhance the conductivity of the systems.
